The passing checkers cover numeric contract matching, edge dtype/stream contracts, tile override legality, AXI stream packing, bandwidth transfer-count exposure, and FIFO authority scope.

The first binding point fixes a conservative Stage 4 DSE contract: lanes=8, fp16 activation/weight paths where specified, fp32 accumulator/residual precision, hidden_size=896, seq_len=16, head_dim=64, num_q_heads=14, num_kv_heads=2, intermediate_size=4864, and per-stage MLP tile_m=16, tile_k=128, tile_n=128.

Global tile_k/tile_m/tile_n values are explicitly defaults only; per-stage tile overrides are authoritative. Stage 4 fifo_depth=16 is a local template default only; Stage 3 edge FIFO buffer depths remain authoritative.

The stream contract trace exposes 13 edges with stream_order token,tile,lane,word. Residual skip paths remain 32-bit, MLP gate/up branch streams into activation_mul remain 16-bit, and block output is 32-bit.

Board memory facts used at this stage are limited to the supplied AXI interface: 512-bit data width, 64-byte alignment, 37-bit address width, one DDR channel, and core-side interface name c0_ddr4_s_axi_*. The total aligned symbolic transfer count is 31,202,816 bytes per layer and 487,544 AXI beats, but this is not real bandwidth or timing evidence.
clock_target_mhz=0 is correctly scoped as unknown shell clock and not timing evidence.

The largest symbolic DSE pressure is in the MLP projection stages, each with 4,358,144 weight elements and about 69,730,304 symbolic compute ops; self_attention has 1,835,008 weight elements and 243,712 symbolic compute ops. These are resource-risk signals only, not implementation estimates.

risks: No current-stage blocking DSE risk is visible after the supplied checker passes; the following are later-stage or handoff risks under the supplied stage_gate_policy.
Later-stage resource/timing risk: symbolic resource_estimate and bandwidth_estimate values cannot prove LUT/DSP/BRAM/URAM use, Fmax, routing, timing closure, or board bandwidth on the real shell.

Later-stage memory/runtime risk: Stage 5 must assign concrete DDR base addresses, address ranges, runtime ABI entries, non-overlap, 64-byte alignment, and transfer reconciliation for residual and branch streams without changing checked stream order or bit widths.

Later-stage implementation risk: generated Chisel/templates must preserve per-stage tile precedence, lanes=8, local FIFO-default scope, dtype casts, residual_precision=32, and stream_order token,tile,lane,word; silent codegen rebinding would invalidate the Stage 4 contract.

Numeric handoff risk: numeric_binding_plan records rounding=nearest_even and saturation=false, while the stage-gate text also preserves a later numeric-policy binding obligation. Before implementation, the evidence bundle should cite the authoritative numeric_policy_id and prevent unapproved rounding or cast changes.

Board-integration risk: shell clock and app-shell target binding are not proven by the Stage 4 artifact. Ambiguous backend target, clock, or shell-interface evidence must trigger bounded approval rather than guessed names.

Verification risk: static parameter checks do not prove leaf operator correctness, connected single-transformer-layer liveness/order, AXI/DDR protocol behavior, or board runtime correctness; the required leaf-to-single-layer-to-board hierarchy must be enforced.
Team-handoff risk: duplicate or overlapping executable actions can create conflicting downstream artifact names unless team_aggregate records a single ordered handoff and acceptance responsibility.
